Exercise A

Read & Spot

Read the dialogue and choose the correct question tag for each gap.

Before you read

This question is not marked - just write what comes to mind.

At the Bus Stop

How it works: a positive sentence gets a negative tag — "You are Jo, aren't you?" A negative sentence gets a positive tag — "You aren't Jo, are you?"

1 Mia: Hi! You are in my English class, I'm Mia.

2 Tom: That's right. You moved here last year,

3 Mia: Yes. The bus is late again,

4 Tom: It will probably be here soon,

5 Mia: You have missed this bus before,

6 Tom: Too often! We could walk to school together tomorrow,

Exercise B

Form the Tag

Eight sentences, eight tenses — only the auxiliary in the tag changes.

Task

1 You are coming to the party,

2 She finished the report,

3 They have never been to Rome,

4 He can swim really well,

5 We will meet at six,

6 It rained all weekend,

7 There is a problem,

8 You would help me,

Exercise C

Tricky Cases

Six sentences where the usual rule needs a second look.

Task

1 I am late,

2 Let's go home,

3 Nobody came to the meeting,

4 You have to leave now,

5 Nothing really matters,

6 Don't be late,

Exercise D

Writing

Write a short dialogue — with at least four question tags.

Task

You and a partner are planning a class trip to the seaside. Write your dialogue (6-8 lines): discuss the bus, the weather, the food and the meeting point. Use at least four question tags — and one tricky case from Exercise C if you can.
